column3: reviewer reading: the grammar/lexical rule the line violates (legacy behaviour is not a criterion)

`while x {}` in an @fn body: the translator's while rule requires `while(...)`; the body is translated only when called (never here), so legacy exits 0; invalid syntax, rejected before running (D-022 #3)
`while x {}` in a lambda block body: translator while rule; lambda never called
`while x {}` in a lambda block body: translator while rule (legacy rejects it when the lambda is called)
`while x {}` in a struct method body: translator while rule
backtick is not a string delimiter in Nift (lexer: only " and '), so the `}` inside the backticks closes the if block and the final `}` is unmatched
`<!-- } -->` is not script syntax; its `}` closes the if block and the final `}` is unmatched
`x := )`: closer without opener
a lone `}` statement
a lone `{` never closed
`fn(f(a,))`: trailing comma leaves an empty parameter
`[a,] := xs`: empty pattern element
`[a, b, ] := xs`: empty pattern element
`[1,2,]`: empty array element
`f(1,)`: empty argument
`[1, 2,]`: empty array element
`(1 +`: `(` never closed (balance is checked first; `+` also lacks a right operand)
`(2 *`: `(` never closed (and `*` lacks a right operand)
`return [1, 2,` (return ends at the line break): `[` unclosed; function never called
`(1 + 2` unclosed in a branch that never runs
lone `}`
`f(1,)`: empty argument
`(1 + 2` unclosed
`(1 + 2` unclosed
lone `}`
`(1 + 2` unclosed
`[1, 2, 3` unclosed (legacy silently drops the rest of the file: Assessment A #1)
`"unterminated` never closed (legacy silently drops the rest: Assessment A #1)
`1, // one` inside a multi-line return value: comments are not expression grammar, so `/` stands where an operand must start (same verdict as the identical multi-line declaration)
